errors.english: The phrase regarding the explanation of the activities means that the results will now be shown.
errors.why: ལས here is the ablative of the root-text lemma 'from these [mahāmudrās] it is explained', not 'activities' (karma).

note: A careful rendering of the commentary on the fruits of the Hūṃkāra mudrās; the deity names and lemma/gloss structure are mostly right.

errors.english: Objects that are endowed with the characteristics of ultimate identity are described in that way
errors.why: The Tibetan says things are called 'one' when they lack a differing function and are taken as bearing the mark of ultimate identity; dropping the 'without a differing function' clause makes it read as if ultimate identity really belongs to them.

note: Follows a difficult lemma-by-lemma Pramāṇa commentary on recognition reasonably well; a few lemma/gloss boundaries are loose.

errors.english: These arise from the consciousness produced by the two conditions of an ordinary person, and from not knowing that the sensations based on that consciousness are without a self.
errors.why: Consciousness and the feeling based on it are both objects of 'not knowing as selfless'; the attachments belong to the ordinary person who does not know this, they do not 'arise from the consciousness'.

fix.find: These arise from the consciousness produced by the two conditions of an ordinary person, and from not knowing that the sensations based on that consciousness are without a self.
fix.replace: They are the attachments of an ordinary person who does not know that the consciousness arising from the two conditions, and the sensations based on it, are without a self.

note: Sound on abhimāna and the two faults; one clause mis-construed.

errors.english: stating "because it is its very self,"
errors.why: ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་རོ completes the reason from the previous side, 'because of being endowed with life-force etc.' (prāṇādimattvāt); there is no reason 'because it is its very self'.

fix.find: stating "because it is its very self,"
fix.replace: stating "because of being endowed with life-force and the like,"

errors.english: This is because even when being "not without a self" is reversed, the existence of the thing would not be established.
errors.why: The Tibetan says that even when selflessness is excluded, the self as a real entity is not thereby established; the English has the double negative excluded and adds a causal 'because'.

fix.find: This is because even when being "not without a self" is reversed, the existence of the thing would not be established.
fix.replace: Even when selflessness is excluded, the self as a real entity would not thereby be established.

errors.english: the self is not established for either [note: referring to both the subject and the example]
errors.why: གཉི་ག here is both parties to the debate (ubhayāsiddha: unestablished for proponent and opponent), not subject and example.

errors.english: assume that "not being without a self" is the same as having a self
errors.why: The concessive says 'even though selflessness itself is absent [there]'; the English invents an assumption by the opponents.

note: The overall point (prāṇādimattva as a kevala-vyatirekin reason without anvaya) comes through, but the opening argument is garbled and several logical clauses are misconstrued.

errors.english: some say it is taught that
errors.why: The whole answer from 'that is true, but...' is the view reported as 'some say'; the English attributes only the last clause to them and presents the rest as the author's own.

errors.english: the power of the blessings of truth, generosity, tranquility, and wisdom
errors.why: These are the four adhiṣṭhānas (foundations/resolves: truth, relinquishment, peace, wisdom); 'blessings' misrenders the technical term.

note: Good on the marks of the feet and the auspicious emblems; attribution of the 'some say' view and one term need correcting.

errors.english: Having become a great scholar, and in order to produce the nectar that counteracts poison as described in the Tantras, he took on the appearance of a peacock.
errors.why: The one who became a great scholar and adopted the peacock guise is the younger brother sent to the scholars, not the yogi of the preceding sentence; the English makes the subject read as the same person.

note: The hagiographical narrative and the verse are rendered clearly; the two brothers' roles blur in one sentence.
Faithful rendering of the Bodhisattvabhūmi commentary on the powers of the bodhisattva and the meaning of bhūmi.

errors.english: Make offerings and praise the chosen deity.
errors.why: With the previous side's མེ་ this is མེ་ཡི་ལྷ, the fire god of the homa, not a chosen (yi dam) deity.

fix.find: Make offerings and praise the chosen deity.
fix.replace: Make offerings and praise the fire god.

errors.english: In this age of expansion and conflict
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'in the fourth age, the time when strife has increased' (kaliyuga), not an 'age of expansion'.

note: Mostly accurate rendering of the end of one sādhana and the opening of a samaya-purification text; the fire-god slip changes the ritual.

errors.english: One should train in accordance with the nature of reality.
errors.why: In this verse (continuing 'the dharma that brings happiness first and last') ཆོས་ཉིད means 'that very dharma/merit', not dharmatā 'the nature of reality'.

note: Faithful rendering of the sūtra quotation on the five gifts of a good person; one term in the verse is over-read.
Accurate rendering of the commentary on the vimokṣa of the beautiful and the four formless liberations.
